intro: Professionals and everyday users convert celsius (°C) to kelvin (K) when working across si and si standards in meteorological weather reports, culinary oven calibration, HVAC setpoints, and clinical thermometry. One celsius equals 274.15 kelvin, while 1 kelvin equals -272.15 celsius. Whether you are verifying temperature specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Temperature Offset vs. Temperature Interval Trap
items: Converting a specific thermometer reading between Celsius (°C) and Kelvin (K) requires applying the zero-point offset (+32 or +273.15). However, when converting a temperature change or difference (ΔT, such as a 10° rise), you must use only the scale ratio (1 °C = 1.8 °F = 1 K) without adding the offset.
Remember that -40 °C and -40 °F are the exact crossover point where both relative scales read the same value.

faqs.question: How many kelvin (K) are in 1 celsius (°C)?
faqs.answer: There are 274.15 kelvin (K) in 1 celsius (°C), which rounds to 274.15 K for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 kelvin equals -272.15 celsius.

faqs.question: How do I convert celsius to kelvin (°C to K)?
faqs.answer: To convert celsius to kelvin, use the formula: K = °C + 273.15. For example, converting 20 °C gives 293.15 K.

faqs.question: What is 20 celsius in kelvin?
faqs.answer: 20 celsius (°C) equals exactly 293.15 kelvin (K) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
